title: Micah Blumberg, AI is the Sword of Revelation (April 1, 2025)
scope: Author publication consulted in full for its theological argument, predictions and metaphorical qualifications; not independent corroboration of its factual or scientific claims.

title: SVGN, News analysis: Trump's AI Fascism is taking shape (June 27, 2026)
scope: The author's published political-theological interpretation. The First/Second Beast passage explicitly uses an allegory; this edition does not independently audit every policy or product claim in the news article.

title: SVGN, Nuclear Deterrence Is the Missing Variable in Eastern Europe (March 1, 2026)
scope: Author publication and its prediction about incentives. It is not evidence of an actual nuclear transfer or a later refinery-to-famine forecast.

title: Revelation 13, World English Bible
scope: Primary scriptural text: two beasts, signs, worship, coercion and buying/selling. A modern identification is an additional interpretation.

title: Galatians 1, World English Bible
scope: Primary text: Paul's account of persecution, revelation, earlier apostles and a visit to Peter and James.

title: 1 Corinthians 15, World English Bible
scope: Primary text: received tradition, named witnesses and the statement that many witnesses remained alive.

title: Biblical Archaeology Society, The Egyptian Vizier Abdiel (June 1, 2018)
scope: Publisher's account of excavator Alain Zivie's research and interpretation of the name Aper-El; read in full. It explicitly does not identify the vizier with Joseph.

title: Alain Zivie, Pharaoh's Man, Abdiel: The Vizier with a Semitic Name
scope: Research article bibliographic record and visible endnotes consulted. Main article is access-restricted; the linguistic interpretation here is reported through the publisher's open account, not a claimed full-text review.

title: Israel Museum, Commentary on Habakkuk
scope: Curator Adolfo D. Roitman's indexed institutional description was retrieved. Direct page loading failed during research. The description says the Teacher, Wicked Priest and Man of Lies are not securely identified.

title: Joseph Blenkinsopp, The Midianite-Kenite Hypothesis Revisited and the Origins of Judah (2008)
scope: Research abstract and visible notes consulted, not the access-restricted main article. The abstract specifies the proposal's textual, poetic, Egyptian-topographical and genealogical foundations.

title: Jacob E. Dunn, A God of Volcanoes: Did Yahwism Take Root in Volcanic Ashes? (2014)
scope: Research abstract consulted, not the access-restricted full article. It combines a southern Midian setting with a volcanic reading of Sinai-Horeb; its existence is not proof of the identification.

title: Exodus 18, World English Bible
scope: Primary text: Jethro, priest of Midian, sacrifice and the meal with Aaron and Israel's elders.

title: Exodus 19, World English Bible
scope: Primary text: smoke, fire, trembling and the Sinai revelation; text description is distinct from a geological identification.

title: University of Chicago, World's oldest weather report could revise Bronze Age chronology (2014)
scope: Institutional account of Robert Ritner and Nadine Moeller's Tempest Stela research; consulted in full. A proposed connection, not a settled date for an Exodus.

title: Hendrik J. Bruins and Johannes van der Plicht, The Minoan Thera eruption predates Pharaoh Ahmose (2025)
scope: Open research paper: abstract and methodological discussion consulted. Multiple Egyptian objects are compared with Thera-context dates; authors conclude Thera predates Ahmose. This edition does not independently reanalyse the numerical dataset.

title: Donald Trump, Republican nomination acceptance address (July 21, 2016)
scope: Full primary speech transcript hosted by the American Presidency Project. Supports the indispensability-rhetoric case, including the same speech's references to working with officials and allies.

title: White House, January 6 clemency proclamation (January 20, 2025)
scope: Primary proclamation read in full. Records named commutations, other pardons and its stated reconciliation rationale. The article describes the dated action, not the present status of every case.

title: U.S. Attorney, Rhodes and Meggs sentencing record (May 25, 2023)
scope: Indexed primary Justice Department release retrieved; direct page loading failed. Its opening records the 2023 seditious-conspiracy sentences and the trial finding about opposing transfer of power. Used only for that historical record, not current case status.

title: Executive Order 14319, Preventing Woke AI in the Federal Government (July 23, 2025)
scope: Primary order read in full. Sections 3 and 4 provide the procurement conditions discussed in the third worked case. This review examines the order as issued, not every later implementing rule or litigation outcome.

title: Timothy H. Lim, The Earliest Commentary on the Prophecy of Habakkuk (2020)
scope: Author's publisher abstract consulted, not the full monograph or a fresh translation of the scroll. Supports the stated alternative interpretation of the Teacher's role and the importance of fidelity to his teachings.

title: Popovic and colleagues, Dating ancient manuscripts using radiocarbon and AI-based writing style analysis (2025)
scope: Published research article consulted in HTML. Used for the distinction between dating manuscript material/handwriting and identifying a historical person. No figure was reproduced and no death date for Jesus or the Teacher was inferred from the model.

title: Galatians 2, World English Bible
scope: Primary text read in full, especially verses 1-10 on an interval, companions and recognized leaders. The passage does not by itself supply an absolute calendar date for the visit.

title: Luke 10, World English Bible
scope: Primary text read in full. Verses 30-37 supply the sequence of practical care discussed in the repair article. Institutional examples are new editorial applications, not reported historical cases.

title: Matthew 5, World English Bible
scope: Primary text read in full. Verses 9, 23-24 and 43-48 support the discussion of peacemaking, reconciliation and enemies. The article separately states its proposed safety and accountability framework.

title: Isaiah 1, World English Bible
scope: Primary text read in full, especially verses 11-17. Supports the contrast between religious performance and the demand to correct wrongdoing and defend vulnerable people.

title: Revelation 21, World English Bible
scope: Primary text read in full, especially verses 1-5. Supports renewal and the end of mourning as part of the narrative, rather than treating destruction as its sole purpose.

title: Luke 22, World English Bible
scope: Primary text consulted, especially 22:42. The article distinguishes the petition and the priority of the Father's will from obedience to a human interpreter.

title: John 5, World English Bible
scope: Primary text consulted, especially 5:30. Supports the contrast between seeking one's own will and the will of the sender.

title: John 6, World English Bible
scope: Primary text consulted, especially 6:38. The contemporary political application is editorial/theological interpretation, not an assertion made by this text.

title: 1 Samuel 8, World English Bible
scope: Primary text read for the warning about what kings take. This is a worked mixed case within the requested comparison, not an exhaustive classification of Samuel.

title: Micah 6, World English Bible
scope: Primary text read for 6:6-8 and the later criticism of dishonest measures and violence. Distinguishes ritual escalation from justice, mercy and humility.

title: Gospel of Thomas, translation by Stephen Patterson and Marvin Meyer
scope: Translation consulted for sayings 1, 3, 12, 13, 39 and 108. The edition uses brief paraphrases and links, not a reproduction of the translation. Translation credit is distinct from an acknowledged influence in the author's older conversations.

title: Library of Congress, The Qumran Community
scope: Curated 1993 exhibition descriptions consulted for Community Rule 4Q258, calendar 4Q321 and MMT 4Q396. These are identified curatorial records, not a new critical edition or the latest dating consensus.

title: Library of Congress, The Qumran Library
scope: Curated exhibition description consulted for Aramaic Enoch 4Q201, dated there to approximately 200-150 BCE. A manuscript witness does not date every Enochic composition or demonstrate a later community's ancestry.

title: James Tabor, A Shared Utopian Vision: Enochians, Essenes, Ebionites, and Nazarenes (July 7, 2026)
scope: The author's short published description was consulted, not the complete video. A later comparison with this wiki's inquiry, not proof that this 2026 page was the source of Micah's 2025 statements.

title: James Tabor, Ebionites, Nazarenes, Essenes, Nasareans: Sorting Out the Names (June 30, 2026)
scope: The author's short post was consulted; the linked interview was not reviewed in full. Similar names are not treated as sufficient evidence of one continuous community.

title: James Tabor, Books
scope: Author-maintained book catalogue consulted to identify works. No claim to have read the complete books in this pass. The Jesus Dynasty is named in an archived author turn; page-level support remains to be added.

title: Donald Trump, August 19, 2025 remarks on ending the war and getting to heaven
scope: Published recording/transcript of the Fox interview excerpt consulted for the reported words, not independent validation of casualty estimates. The quoted speaker links ending the war to heaven; he does not explicitly explain his concern as putting his own will above God's. That further explanation is identified as the author's theological inference.

title: Genesis 14:18-20, World English Bible
scope: Primary chapter consulted. The encounter, blessing and tithe are kept separate from later lineage claims.

title: Psalm 110, World English Bible
scope: Primary psalm consulted, especially verses 1-7. Royal and judicial language is retained alongside the priestly address.

title: Hebrews 7, World English Bible
scope: Primary chapter consulted, especially verses 1-17 and 23-28. Textual resemblance, descent and continuing priesthood are distinguished.

title: Logan Williams (2023), Melchizedek, the Son of Man, and Eschatological Jubilee
scope: Full-text HTML consulted, particularly the author's translation of 11Q13 II 2-9 and discussion of II 6 and 13. His active-agent reading is distinguished from the critical edition he disputes. The critical edition itself has not been collated in this pass. This is current editorial research, not a recovered author acknowledgment.

title: Melchizedek, translated by Soren Giversen and Birger A. Pearson
scope: Online translation retrieved in the indexed full-text result; direct-page retrieval failed. Marked lacunae are retained in the interpretation. The online notice requests published-edition citations for academic work; printed page/line collation remains open. Credit is for a textual source used by this edition, not a claimed personal influence on Micah.
